title: Managing Labels in a Fraud Detection Context

cues.en: Welcome to Section two Introduction to Fraud Detection.
cues.zh: 歡迎來到第二章：詐欺偵測簡介。

cues.en: This is Lecture six, where we look at managing labels within a fraud detection context.
cues.zh: 這是第六堂課，我們要看看詐欺偵測情境下如何處理標籤。

cues.en: So in the Notebook I've replicated the steps from the previous lesson we have just read in the CSV as a data frame and within fraud.
cues.zh: 我在 Notebook 重複了上一堂課的步驟，將 CSV 讀入成 DataFrame。在詐欺偵測中，

cues.en: What we are frequently interested in finding out is how many fraudulent records do exist from a historical perspective.
cues.zh: 我們經常想知道，歷史紀錄中究竟有多少筆詐欺交易。

cues.en: Right.
cues.zh: 對吧。

cues.en: So we know that the number of fraudulent records can be identified by looking at this class column, which is the label from a machine learning perspective.
cues.zh: 我們可以查看 Class 這個欄位來確認詐欺紀錄數量；從機器學習的角度看，它就是標籤。

cues.en: And in Pandas, we can actually just select that column and then apply this value Counts method on it,
cues.zh: 在 pandas 中，選取這個欄位後，直接套用 value_counts 方法，

cues.en: which works nicely in the sense that it gives us an output where the unique values within that column
cues.zh: 就能得到很實用的輸出：它會把欄位中的不同值

cues.en: have a kind of a group by with a count applied to them.
cues.zh: 分組，並計算每個值的出現次數。

cues.en: So we know all of the records with a zero within the class column.
cues.zh: 所以，Class 欄位為 0 的所有紀錄，

cues.en: There are 284,000 of them and those with a one which are the confirmed fraudulent records.
cues.zh: 共有約 284,000 筆；而值為 1 的，就是已確認的詐欺紀錄。

cues.en: There are 492.
cues.zh: 這些共有 492 筆。

cues.en: So previously when I mentioned a severe class imbalance, we can see that, you know, 284,000 versus
cues.zh: 先前提過嚴重的類別不平衡；現在可以看到，約 284,000 筆對上

cues.en: 492 is quite significant, especially when it comes to a machine learning problem.
cues.zh: 492 筆，差距非常大，對機器學習問題尤其重要。

cues.en: I'll explain to you why that is.
cues.zh: 接下來說明原因。

cues.en: So if we are training a model, what we're going to find is that our algorithm that we use would very
cues.zh: 訓練模型時，我們使用的演算法

cues.en: likely become overwhelmed and biased towards the majority class, which is the normal class.
cues.zh: 很可能受到多數類別主導，而偏向正常交易這一類。

cues.en: So it might end up learning patterns of the majority class only while neglecting to pick up much on
cues.zh: 結果可能只學會多數類別的模式，卻沒有學到多少

cues.en: the the minority class.
cues.zh: 少數類別的特徵。

cues.en: And that would be a problem.
cues.zh: 這會造成問題。

cues.en: And we'd see that when we actually evaluate the performance of the model.
cues.zh: 等到實際評估模型效能時，就會看出來。

cues.en: All right.
cues.zh: 好。

cues.en: So we wouldn't be able to learn anything meaningful from the minority class, but we can cater for this imbalance.
cues.zh: 我們可能無法從少數類別學到有意義的資訊，不過，這種類別不平衡是可以處理的。

cues.en: There are a number of ways to do this.
cues.zh: 處理方式有好幾種。

cues.en: One of them is to up sample the minority class at training time.
cues.zh: 其中之一，是在訓練時對少數類別進行上採樣。

cues.en: So we've got our set of training data.
cues.zh: 也就是在訓練資料中，

cues.en: You know, there might be a few hundred instances of fraud, but can we use techniques to generate synthetic copies of that?
cues.zh: 可能只有幾百筆詐欺案例，那能不能用某些技術，合成出更多這類樣本？

cues.en: You know, there are a number of approaches.
cues.zh: 這方面有幾種方法。

cues.en: One of the popular approaches is smote, you know, which is synthetic oversampling of the minority
cues.zh: 其中一種常見方法是 SMOTE，也就是對少數

cues.en: class.
cues.zh: 類別進行合成過採樣。

cues.en: Right?
cues.zh: 對吧？

cues.en: That's one approach.
cues.zh: 這是一種方法。

cues.en: Another is to down sample the majority class.
cues.zh: 另一種是對多數類別進行下採樣。

cues.en: So that's to say, well, if I've got 284,000 good records, can't I just cut that number in half, make it 100,000 or make it 10,000?
cues.zh: 也就是說，如果有 284,000 筆正常紀錄，能不能減半，或減到 100,000 筆，甚至 10,000 筆？

cues.en: And, you know, let's train a model and see if that solves the issue.
cues.zh: 接著訓練模型，看看是否解決問題。

cues.en: Right?
cues.zh: 對吧？

cues.en: So that's the second approach.
cues.zh: 這是第二種方法。

cues.en: And a third approach might be to use a different modelling technique.
cues.zh: 第三種方法，則是採用不同的建模技術。

cues.en: So there are approaches called anomaly detection algorithms specifically to solve these kinds of problems.
cues.zh: 有一類稱為異常偵測的演算法，專門處理這類問題。

cues.en: Normally these are prepared or they are trained in an unsupervised fashion, meaning they're trained without labels.
cues.zh: 它們通常採非監督式方式建構或訓練，也就是訓練時不使用標籤。

cues.en: You save all of your labels for the testing phase of the modeling process, and then you can evaluate
cues.zh: 你把所有標籤留到建模流程的測試階段，

cues.en: the effectiveness after you've trained the model in an unsupervised fashion.
cues.zh: 等模型完成非監督式訓練後，再評估成效。

cues.en: So that's one of the ways that you can solve it.
cues.zh: 這也是解決問題的方式之一。

cues.en: Lastly, what you can do is rebalance the classes at training time using the algorithms, class weights, hyper parameter.
cues.zh: 最後，如果演算法有提供 class_weight 超參數，也可以在訓練時利用它來平衡類別。

cues.en: If it does have one to penalize the loss function more for misclassifications made on the minority class.
cues.zh: 讓少數類別的錯誤分類，在損失函數中受到更重的懲罰。

cues.en: All right.
cues.zh: 好。

cues.en: So what that means is when the model is learning from its mistakes, if there's misclassifications,
cues.zh: 也就是說，模型在從錯誤中學習時，如果出現錯誤分類，

cues.en: you're going to penalize those instances for the minority class a lot more than you're going to penalize it for the majority class.
cues.zh: 少數類別的錯誤就會比多數類別的錯誤受到更大的懲罰。

cues.en: Basically telling your algorithm to pay more attention to the minority class, you know, don't get it wrong, learn more about it.
cues.zh: 等於告訴演算法要多留意少數類別，別再分錯，要更仔細學習它。

cues.en: And that has proven to work quite well in a supervised learning context as well.
cues.zh: 這在監督式學習的情境下，也已證明是相當有效的方法。
